previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of idiopathic chronic pancreatitis was admitted for an acute flare characterized by persistent epigastric pain radiating to the back, nausea, and inability to tolerate oral intake. Despite normal lipase levels, her symptoms were consistent with prior episodes. She was managed with bowel rest, IV fluids, and IV hydromorphone for pain control. Her condition improved over three days, allowing transition to sips on hospital day two and clear liquids on day three. She was successfully switched back to her home oral pain and anti-nausea medications and tolerated oral intake without complications. Her chronic conditions, including depression, overactive bladder, GERD, and stable iron deficiency anemia, were maintained on baseline therapy. She was discharged home with instructions to slowly advance her diet, continue her medication regimen, and follow up with her GI specialist and primary care provider.

radiology_notes.text:
PICC LINE PLACEMENT

INDICATION:  IV access needed for ___ woman with chronic pancreatitis,
here with poor p.o. intake and potentially needing TPN.

The procedure was explained to the patient.  A timeout was performed.

RADIOLOGIST:  Dr. ___ performed the procedure.Dr ___
___.

TECHNIQUE:  Using sterile technique and local anesthesia, the right brachial
vein was punctured under direct ultrasound guidance using a micropuncture set.
Ultrasound images were obtained before and immediately after establishing
intravenous access.  A peel-away sheath was then placed over a guidewire .Mild
stenosis of the right subclavian / brachiocephalic vein junction was noted on
contrast injection but was easily crossed with a glidewire.
A double lumen PICC line measuring 30 cm in length was then placed through the
peel-away sheath with its tip eventually  positioned in the SVC under
fluoroscopic guidance. Position of the catheter was confirmed by a
fluoroscopic spot film of the chest.

The peel-away sheath and guidewire were then removed.  The catheter was
secured to the skin, flushed, and a sterile dressing applied.

The patient tolerated the procedure well.  There were no immediate
complications.

IMPRESSION:  
Ultrasound and fluoroscopically guided double lumen PICC line placement via
the right brachial venous approach. Mild stenosis of the right subclavian /
brachiocephalic vein junction was noted  
Final internal length is 30 cm, with the tip positioned in SVC.  
The line is ready to use.

HISTORY:  Evaluation for air fluid levels in a patient with chronic
pancreatitis and a history of adhesions.

COMPARISON:  Abdominal radiograph ___.

FINDINGS: Upright and supine frontal abdominal radiographs demonstrate
nondilated loops of small and large bowel with no abnormal air-fluid levels. 
There is a moderate amount of stool in the colon.  No free intraperitoneal air
is identified.

IMPRESSION:  No abnormal air-fluid levels. No evidence of obstruction.
